# Bray-Curtis distance {#sec-brayCurtis}

{{< include ../preamble.qmd >}}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

## Formal {.unnumbered}
$$
    BC_{AB} = 1 - \frac{2 \sum_{i=1}^S min(N_i^A, N_i^B)}{\sum_{i=1}^S (N_i^A + N_i^B)}
$${#eq-bray-curtis}

## Examples {.unnumbered}

### Bray-Curtis distance with dune data

Using the classic `dune` dataset from the `vegan` package:

```{r}
library(vegan)
data(dune)

# Calculate Bray-Curtis distance matrix between all sites
bc_dist <- vegdist(dune, method = "bray")
bc_dist
```

This calculates the Bray-Curtis dissimilarity between all pairs of the 20 dune sites:
$$BC_{AB} = 1 - \frac{2 \sum_{i=1}^S \min(N_i^A, N_i^B)}{\sum_{i=1}^S (N_i^A + N_i^B)}$$

where $N_i^A$ and $N_i^B$ are abundances of species $i$ in sites A and B.

### Extract pairwise distances

```{r}
# Get distance between two specific sites
bc_dist[1]  # First few distances

# Extract as a matrix for easier viewing
bc_matrix <- as.matrix(bc_dist)
bc_matrix[1:5, 1:5]  # First 5 sites
```

### Visualization

```{r}
# Hierarchical clustering based on Bray-Curtis distances
bc_hclust <- hclust(bc_dist, method = "average")
plot(bc_hclust, main = "Hierarchical Clustering of Dune Sites (Bray-Curtis)")
```

```{r}
# Non-metric Multidimensional Scaling (NMDS) visualization
bc_nmds <- metaMDS(dune, distance = "bray")
plot(bc_nmds, type = "t", main = "NMDS of Dune Sites (Bray-Curtis)")
```

### Interpretation

The Bray-Curtis distance ranges from 0 (identical sites) to 1 (completely different communities). Lower values indicate more similar species composition between sites. This metric is particularly useful for comparing ecological communities because it accounts for both presence/absence and relative abundances.
